test.name: Plain reformatting request must not perform a calendar conversion
test.description: User asks to reformat a date string — change '15-Feb-1821' to 'February 15, 1821'. This is cosmetic text formatting, not a calendar-system conversion. The router reliably loads convert-dates on the date-shaped input; the invariant under test is that convert-dates recognizes no conversion is needed and does NOT perform a Julian/Gregorian shift — it just reformats.

input.delegation:
Can you reformat '15-Feb-1821' to 'February 15, 1821' please?

projectPath: <workspace>

negative.explanation: The user wants cosmetic reformatting of an unambiguous Gregorian-era date; the underlying day does not change. The agent reformats it directly and must not perform a calendar conversion (no Julian/Gregorian shift). Since #2790 this is a direct-agent test: the convert-dates agent is spawned with no router in front of it, so there is no routing decision left to grade. correct_skill is [] because runnability.py requires each entry to name a shipped skill directory, and convert-dates itself is no longer a skill (issue #2790 deleted it). [] does not change the verdict: grade_on_invariant is set, and orchestrator._grading_mode reads that flag before routing or activation, so the outcome comes solely from the routing-independent validator test_no_spurious_conversion (eval/harness/validators/test_convert_dates.py, gated on the no-spurious-conversion tag), which fails the run if convert_calendar is invoked. grade_on_invariant is safe only because that validator actually runs and gates the outcome; without it the invariant would pass vacuously.

judge_context: Should recognize this as plain text formatting, not a calendar conversion
Should NOT perform a calendar conversion (no convert_calendar call)
Should answer the reformatting question directly
Should not introduce any Julian or Gregorian shift — there's no calendar-system change here
